title: Farmers and environmental groups protest Omnibus X pesticide reform in Strasbourg

tea.why: Protesters oppose the European Commission's 'Omnibus X' legislative package, which aims to simplify pesticide authorization rules.
tea.want: They demand that MEPs reject the proposed reform, fearing it will weaken health and environmental safeguards.
tea.changed: Nov 24: Hundreds of protesters gathered outside the European Parliament to oppose the removal of fixed expiry dates for pesticide approvals.

summary: On November 24, 2026, hundreds of farmers, scientists, and environmental activists demonstrated outside the European Parliament in Strasbourg. The protest, supported by over 360 organizations from across Europe, targeted the European Commission's proposed 'Omnibus X' legislative package. Critics argue that the reform, which seeks to simplify the authorization process for pesticides, would remove fixed expiry dates and weaken protections for public health and the environment. Protesters expressed concerns that the changes could allow harmful substances to remain on the market indefinitely. The European Commission maintains that the current system is hindered by excessive bureaucracy and that the reform would generate significant cost savings. The European Parliament is expected to determine its position on the proposal before the end of the year.
demands: Reject the Omnibus X legislative package
Maintain fixed expiry dates for pesticide approvals
response: The European Commission stated that the current authorization system is blocked by bureaucracy and argued that the legislative package would save over one billion euros annually for companies and national administrations.

crowd.text: Around 350 people attended, with organisers claiming 500.

updates.text: Hundreds of protesters gathered outside the European Parliament in Strasbourg to oppose the Omnibus X pesticide reform.
